children: Oil and gas producer HighPeak Energy
will be reporting earnings this Monday after market hours. Here’s what you need to know.

HighPeak Energy beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $272.4 million, up 25.8% year on year. It was an incredible quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is HighPeak Energy a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting HighPeak Energy’s revenue to grow 33.4% year on year, a reversal from the 30.5% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. HighPeak Energy has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at HighPeak Energy’s peers in the u.s. shale e&p segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Crescent Energy delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 55.9%, beating analysts’ expectations by 3.5%, and Matador Resources reported revenues up 23.8%, topping estimates by 5.5%. Crescent Energy traded down 3.4% following the results while Matador Resources was also down 7.3%.

In the last twelve months or so, the market has shifted its attention from one area of macro importance to the next (AI disintermediation and AI capex spending to geopolitical conflict, rates, and whether the economy is on solid footing or not). While some of the u.s. shale e&p stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 10.8% on average over the last month. HighPeak Energy is down 25.3% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $10 (compared to the current share price of $7.13).
